questions.question: Describe the parts of a ratchet and pawl and explain why it allows rotation in one direction only.
questions.expected_answer: A ratchet is a wheel with saw-shaped teeth, each having a long sloping face and a short steep face; a pawl is an arm pivoted near the wheel and pressed into the teeth by a spring or gravity. Turning the wheel in the free direction brings the sloping faces under the pawl, which rides up each slope and drops into the next gap with a click. Turning the other way brings a steep face against the pawl tip, which cannot ride over it; the load pushes the pawl further into the tooth and the wheel is locked. The ratchet controls direction and neither adds force nor changes speed.

questions.question: Give three applications of the ratchet and pawl and state the purpose it serves in each.
questions.expected_answer: A boat trailer winch: the ratchet stops the drum spinning back under the boat's weight when the handle is released, and lifting the pawl lets the boat down. A ratchet socket spanner: the pawl drives the socket on the push stroke and freewheels on the return so the socket never leaves the nut, with a lever to reverse direction. A cable tie or handbrake lever: a straight or curved ratchet holds the strap or lever at any tightened position and prevents it loosening until the pawl is released.

questions.question: Explain how a ratchet would be evaluated for fitness for purpose and safety, and describe one weakness of the mechanism.
questions.expected_answer: Fitness for purpose: it must hold the load reliably at any position and release easily when the operator wants it to, so a release lever is essential. Safety: the pawl must be hardened steel, strong enough to carry the full load on one tooth, and pivoted so the load pushes it into engagement rather than out; a slipping pawl lets a winch handle spin back and injure the operator. Ergonomics and cost also apply: one-handed release and a hard-wearing pawl. A weakness is that it holds only at a tooth, allowing slight backward movement before locking, so fine teeth are used where precise holding matters.
